Thursday will mark my 6 month anniversary of being cigarette free. On a whim, my wife picked up an Aspire starter kit while at the tobacco store because I had expressed interest in it. I put it together the next morning, and haven't had a cigarette since. Three days later, my wife had her own and hasn't smoked a cigarette since. A week after she got her Aspire, we decided to upgrade our equipment to something better. I got the MVP 3.0 and a Kanger Subtank, and she got a 30 watt eleaf iStick and a Kanger Subtank mini. That really sealed the deal on quitting. Getting more vapor without feeling like my cheeks were going to collapse made all the difference. Now we each have multiple mods, tanks, drippers and have a tremendous amount of fun experimenting with making our own juices. Even with treating ourselves to new equipment, buying every flavor that tickles our fancy, we're saving tons of money from not buying cigarettes or cigarette making supplies (we made our own with a cigarette injector for 6 years).

Like the guy in the article, I tried many different ways to quit: patches, gum, lozenges, hypnosis, wellbutrin, and Chantix. I was a 2+ pack a day smoker for 27 years and quitting the cigs was painless using a vape, and quite pleasant in fact.

We just absolutely love hearing all of these success stories. It makes it so much easier to come to work every day when we keep hearing positive news and stories like this. Congrats to you and the wife getting off of cigarettes.

With all the negative press vaping seems to get it is important we get more stories like this out there. Hopefully the media will pick up on it one day soon and start publishing more positive articles concerning vaping. Please, feel free to submit your story to our blog. We love getting success stories! Cheers, and vape on!
